Kind of cool isn't it? It's not just these fungi though, there's a bunch of bacteria and other microorganisms that form symbiotic relationships with the root zone. Trichoderma and bacillus bacteria come to mind off the top of my head.

A plant could grow with just nutrients and water but it's so much more susceptible to foreign disease and it really matters what pH the root zone is in to ensure proper nutrient uptake.

With these added fungi and bacteria the root zone is sort of regulated to some extent. by sending signals to the root zone the fungus can release the nutrients required - and these organisms can operate in a much larger range of pH. Not to mention that the mycorryhzea blows up the root system to cover massive areas.

I used to grow flowers and herbs and once I started using beneficial bacteria I've never had a single problem. Pretty cool stuff.

The mycelium also allow for the tree's to talk with each other, then tree's with extra food use the mycelium to pass valuable nutrients to younger tree's that might not get as much sun.

So, our thoughts of "Survival of the fittest", does not really apply to tree's in a forest type setting.
